title: Unexpected PySpark filter behaviour
question:
I want to filter out the rows where CID (string type) is '-' and trait_diff is null. The codes I have provided are filtering out the rows where both of them are null even if I do not put isNull for CID (Like in 3rd line of code).

df = df.filter(
    ~((col('CID') == "-") & (col('CID').isNull()) & col('trait_diff').isNull())
)

df = df.filter(
    ~((col('CID').isNull()) & col('trait_diff').isNull())
)

df = df.filter(
    ~((col('CID') == "-") & col('trait_diff').isNull())
)

Above 3 code filter out the same rows where CID is null and trait_diff is null regardless if CID of being null is not present. I have checked it filters out 3 rows in all cases and it is where both of these are null.

In the first, I can't understand how CID could be '-' and null at the same time. When removing the ~ to get the 3 filtered out rows, it does not return anything. (to check what rows are getting filtered, I exported the excel file, databricks did not return anything)

I have also tried out this one exactly the same behaviour as above ones.

df = df.filter(
    (col('CID') != "-") | col('trait_diff').isNotNull()
)

Can anybody help me out here understanding why it does not give expected results.

This one seems to work giving out expected number of rows, no idea why this works (because if CID is '-' and it is not null and we do not need to put this condition in) and not others

df = df.filter(
    ~((col('CID') == "-") & col('CID').isNotNull() & col('trait_diff').isNull())
)
answer:
I want to filter out the rows where CID (string type) is '-' and trait_diff is null.

Unfortunately, English is not compliant with computer logic. Therefore, when you say that, it could mean two different things:

  1. You want to remove the rows where CID == '-' and then remove the rows where trait_diff is null.
  2. You want to remove rows where both CID == '-' and trait_diff is null at the same time.

In the first case, you will remove more rows than in the second one. Additionally, null will always return False when you test it. If you want to handle nulls properly, you need to use an equality that is null-safe: eqNullSafe.

Create an Example:

from pyspark.sql.functions import col

data = [
    ["a", "a"],
    ["a", None],
    ["-", "a"],
    ["-", None],
    [None, "a"],
    [None, None],
]

columns = ["CID", "trait_diff"]

df = spark.createDataFrame(data, columns)

df.show()
CID trait_diff
a a
a null
- a
- null
null a
null null

Remove Rows, First Case:

df.filter((col("CID") != "-") & col("trait_diff").isNotNull()).show()
CID trait_diff
a a

OR with safe null handling

df.filter(~col("CID").eqNullSafe("-") & col("trait_diff").isNotNull()).show()
CID trait_diff
a a
null a

Remove Rows, Second Case:

df.filter((col("CID") != "-") | col("trait_diff").isNotNull()).show()
CID trait_diff
a a
a null
- a
null a

OR with safe null handling

df.filter(~col("CID").eqNullSafe("-") | col("trait_diff").isNotNull()).show()
CID trait_diff
a a
a null
- a
null a
null null
